result.title: EgoCARBS: Egocentric Video Meets Active Acoustics for Kitchen Action Understanding
result.comment: 36 pages (12 main paper and references, 24 supplementary material). Project page: https://saif-mahmud.github.io/projects/ego-carbs
result.summary: Egocentric video records what a person looks at, but often misses what their body does: the hands leave the frame, and arm motion goes unseen. An exocentric camera recovers this context, but it must be installed wherever the activity happens. Active acoustic sensing can recover it from the wearables themselves: a device's speaker emits inaudible chirps, and its microphone senses the motion of the hands, arms, and nearby objects from their echoes. Yet no public dataset pairs it with egocentric video. We present EgoCARBS, with two deliverables. The first is a multimodal dataset and benchmark: 15 participants cook unscripted meals in their own kitchens wearing camera glasses and an off-the-shelf smartwatch that both sense with active acoustics, synchronized with egocentric and exocentric video and the watch's audio and IMU, with 4,019 verb-noun action annotations in 11.4 hours. The second is a study of what the wearables add to egocentric video. On verb recognition, they add at least as much as an exocentric camera for participants seen in training, and even more for new participants, for whom the exocentric camera does not help. Active acoustics alone provides most of this gain, and helps most where the camera does not see the hands. Trimmed action recognition, detection, and anticipation remain open. We will release the data, our data collection and annotation tools, and pre-trained models.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 EgoCARBS：将自中心视频与智能手表的主动声学感知（扬声器发出人耳不可闻的 chirp、由回声感知手部与物体运动）配对，构建 11.4 小时、4,019 条动词-名词标注的厨房动作数据集与基准，并分析可穿戴传感相对外中心相机对动词识别的增益。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「相机看不到手时用主动声学补足证据」的思路，可能与 LVR 中证据获取与多通道证据筛选的问题形成概念类比，可供核查；但论文不涉及 latent 推理状态，联系较远。
